gaps.sentence: They chose a guide on ___ they could rely completely.
gaps.hint: rely on somebody — person after preposition
gaps.explanation: After the preposition 'on', the person takes 'whom'; 'which' is only for things.

gaps.sentence: The house ___ stands on the corner dates from 1870.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' is needed because a house is a thing; 'where' would introduce information about location, not a subject.

gaps.sentence: The manager, for ___ the team played so hard, thanked everyone.
gaps.hint: played for the manager — person after preposition
gaps.explanation: The preposition 'for' demands the object form 'whom' for a person.

gaps.sentence: She was two hours late, ___ annoyed the interviewer.
gaps.hint: comment on the whole situation before the comma
gaps.explanation: When a clause comments on the whole previous statement, use 'which' after the comma.

gaps.sentence: All ___ I want is a quiet weekend at home.
gaps.explanation: After 'all' the relative pronoun is 'that' (often omitted); 'all what' is always wrong.

gaps.sentence: His latest film, ___ was shot entirely in Iceland, won three awards.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' is the subject pronoun for the film; 'that' never appears in non-defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: Nobody knows the reason ___ he resigned so suddenly.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why ...' is the standard pattern; 'why' means 'for which'.

gaps.sentence: That was the year ___ the company nearly went bankrupt.
gaps.hint: time: it happened in that year
gaps.explanation: 'When' is used after 'the year'; 'which' would need 'in which'.
